entry.reasons: The entry is factually correct and directly matches the wording of Essential Knowledge 3.5.A.5: 'As input values increase, the graphs of sinusoidal functions oscillate between concave down and concave up.' The topic code is correct and no caution is needed.

The body matches essential knowledge 3.5.A.5: “As input values increase, the graphs of sinusoidal functions oscillate between concave down and concave up.” Topic 3.5 is the correct owner and topic code. The singular phrasing does not change the meaning, so no caution is needed.

a_factual: The body matches 3.5.A.5 almost verbatim: "As input values increase, the graphs of sinusoidal functions oscillate between concave down and concave up." The entry says "the graph of a sinusoidal function" instead of "the graphs of sinusoidal functions", but the substance is identical. b_topic_codes: 3.5.A.5 first appears under Topic 3.5 (Sinusoidal Functions), so owner_topic_code "3.5" is correct, and topic_codes ["3.5"] is the only topic that uses it. c_ced_required: Topic 3.5 Learning Objective 3.5.A ("Identify key characteristics of the sine and cosine functions") is supported by 3.5.A.5, so students are required to know this. d_caution: The entry's wording is essentially the point-earning wording, so no caution is needed and caution null is correct. unit_number 3 matches the CED Unit 3 pages.

The entry accurately represents the reciprocal relationship between period and frequency as defined in EK 3.5.A.2, including the specific values for the parent sine and cosine functions. Topic 3.5 is the correct owner topic, and Topic 3.7 also utilizes these concepts for modeling.

3.5.A.2 states, “The period and frequency of a sinusoidal function are reciprocals,” and gives period 2π and frequency 1/(2π) for sine and cosine. Topic 3.5 first requires this relationship; 3.7.A.1 also uses period and frequency in sinusoidal modeling. The wording needs no caution.

a_factual: CED 3.5.A.2 reads 'The period and frequency of a sinusoidal function are reciprocals. The period of f(θ) = sin θ and g(θ) = cos θ is 2π, and the frequency is 1/2π.' The body gives frequency = 1/period and period = 1/frequency, and for sin θ and cos θ gives period 2π and frequency 1/(2π). This matches the CED. b_topic_codes: 3.5.A.2 first appears in Topic 3.5 (Sinusoidal Functions), so owner_topic_code 3.5 is correct. Topic 3.7 uses the same relationship in 3.7.A.1 ('can be used to determine or estimate the period and frequency for a sinusoidal function model'), so listing 3.7 is valid. c_ced_required: 3.5.A.2 requires students to know the period–frequency reciprocal relationship and to apply it to sine and cosine. d_caution: the entry's title and formula are a close restatement of the CED wording, which uses 'reciprocals' and gives the sine/cosine values explicitly. The point-earning idea is carried by the entry, so no caution is needed and caution null is correct.

The formulas accurately represent the reciprocal relationships defined in Topic 3.11 (specifically 3.11.A.1, 3.11.A.2, and 3.11.A.4) including the correct domain restrictions (where the denominators are non-zero).

CED 3.11.A.1–3.11.A.4 defines secant as the reciprocal of cosine, cosecant as the reciprocal of sine, and cotangent as the reciprocal of tangent or cos θ/sin θ, with the stated domain restrictions. Topic 3.11 first requires these definitions; Topic 3.12 uses equivalent trigonometric forms, including tan²θ = sec²θ − 1 (3.12.A.2). The formulas express the CED definitions directly, so no caution is needed.

a_factual: The body matches the CED exactly. 3.11.A.1 defines sec θ as "the reciprocal of the cosine function, where cos θ ≠ 0"; 3.11.A.2 defines csc θ as "the reciprocal of the sine function, where sin θ ≠ 0"; 3.11.A.4 defines cot θ as "the reciprocal of the tangent function, where tan θ ≠ 0. Equivalently, cot θ = cos θ / sin θ, where sin θ ≠ 0." All domain conditions and symbols match. b_topic_codes: 3.11 is the unit's topic that first requires sec/csc/cot (3.11.A.1–A.4). 3.12 uses sec in 3.12.A.2 ("tan²θ = sec²θ − 1"), so listing 3.12 is supported. c_ced_required: 3.11.A.1–3.11.A.4 require students to identify key characteristics of these functions as defined through reciprocals and quotients, so the definitions are required content. d_caution: The CED's point-earning wording is "reciprocal of ..." with the stated restrictions. The entry presents the same reciprocal definitions as formulas with the same restrictions and includes the cos/sin equivalent that the CED states explicitly, so the formula form earns the same point and no caution is needed.

The formula correctly relates the parameter b to frequency using the reciprocal relationship of period and frequency (3.5.A.2) and the period formula (3.6.A.6). The caution correctly notes that b can be negative as 3.6.A.1 allows any nonzero real b.

The relationship is mathematically valid, and Topics 3.6 and 3.7 use period and frequency to describe and construct sinusoidal models. But the entry does not reproduce the formula as printed in 3.6.A.6: the CED gives the period as (1/b)2π, not 2π/|b|. The caution explains why the magnitude matters for negative b, but does not alert readers to that substantive difference from the cited CED wording.

3.5.A.2 states that period and frequency are reciprocals. 3.6.A.6 gives the sinusoidal period as 2π/b, while 3.6.A.1 permits any nonzero real b; because a period is positive, the formula uses |b| when b may be negative. Topic 3.6 first introduces the parameter b, and 3.7.A.1 uses period and frequency to construct sinusoidal models. The caution correctly explains the magnitude and sign distinction.

a_factual: The CED states the two inputs. 3.5.A.2 says period and frequency 'are reciprocals', and 3.6.A.6 gives period '(1/b)2π' with b a nonzero real (3.6.A.1). Algebra gives |b| = 2π·frequency. The body's |b| is correct because the period in 3.1.B.1 is a positive smallest value. The exact formula is not printed in the CED but follows directly from the stated relations. b_topic_codes: 3.6 is the first topic where b appears in the period expression (3.6.A.6), so it is the correct owner. 3.7 uses frequency for model construction in 3.7.A.1, so listing it is valid. c_ced_required: 3.7.A.1 requires determining or estimating period and frequency for a sinusoidal model, and 3.6.A.6 requires the period-to-b relation. Converting a given frequency to b is the step needed to build that model, so the CED requires it implicitly. d_caution: The caution correctly warns against setting b equal to frequency or period, and its example is correct (200 cycles/s gives |b| = 400π). It also correctly notes that b may be negative, which 3.6.A.1 permits (any nonzero real b). The caution is present and needed because the body's wording (|b|) differs from the CED's signed (1/b)2π form.
